title: None of the three code/ smoke tests are real pytest tests, and none are in the validation loop
description: All three files are named test_*.py (which signals a pytest suite) but define ZERO test_-prefixed functions: test_provenance_smoke.py and test_cross_modal_alignment.py put their whole body at module top level, and test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py wraps everything in main(). pytest collects 0 test items from any of them. Worse, pytest.ini pins testpaths=tests (pytest.ini:2), so the canonical validation loop `pytest tests/` never even looks at code/. These files therefore contribute nothing to the safe validation loop and give a false impression of test coverage for the M7 provenance/alignment/ordinal code paths (which the repo-root tests/ suite does NOT exercise — it only tests the legacy bi-modal package).
evidence: pytest.ini:2 `testpaths = tests`; grep for `def test_` across the three files returns nothing; test_provenance_smoke.py has statements at module scope lines 17-110; test_cross_modal_alignment.py lines 67-169; test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py logic is inside main() (line 22) under a __main__ guard (line 83).
fix: Convert each smoke script into pytest test_* functions (assertions inside functions, no work at import), add a __main__ guard, and relocate the dataset-free ones (provenance + alignment, both CPU/dummy-data) into tests/ so `pytest tests/` actually runs them. Keep dataset/checkpoint-dependent ordinal logic out of the default collection or mark it skip/xfail with a clear reason.

title: Entire smoke test executes at import time (no __main__ guard, no functions)
description: There is no `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard and no functions; every statement (lines 17-110) runs the moment the module is imported. That includes constructing the model and running one epoch of ContinualLearner.train_task plus several evaluate() calls. Importing the module IS running the smoke test, so any pytest collection or plain `import` executes training, and a failed assertion surfaces as an import/collection error rather than a clean test failure. VERIFIED SAFE regarding the 4-5h trap: it forces device='cpu' (line 31) and uses DummyLoader random tensors (lines 36-54), and its only heavy import m7_trimodal_run_provenance is __main__-guarded (that module, line 1378) and does not import the unguarded m7_trimodal_run — so importing this file does NOT download datasets or start the long run. The problem is purely that import==execution.
evidence: No `if __name__` / `def ` in file; top-level executable statements lines 17-34 and 52-110; device forced cpu at line 31; DummyLoader defined lines 36-54.
fix: Wrap the body in test functions (e.g. test_random_init_baseline, test_zero_shot_near_chance) and a __main__ guard so importing/collecting the module does not execute training.

title: Assertion tolerance (<8.0 pp) contradicts the success message it prints (~3pp)
description: Line 62 asserts `abs(ri - chance) < 8.0` but line 63 prints `All random-init baselines within ~3pp of chance`. The asserted bound (8.0 pp) is nearly 3x the claimed bound (3 pp), so the printed claim is not what the code checks. The 8.0 is also a magic tolerance with no derivation, and it is statistically under-powered: each random_init_baseline evaluates on DummyLoader(10, ...) which yields 10 batches x 4 = ~40 samples (lines 52-54, 42-48), averaged over n_seeds=2 (line 59). At that sample size an accuracy estimate has a large spread, so the 8.0 bound is arbitrary and can occasionally fail spuriously. Under the repo's RULE-1 culture, printing 'within ~3pp' while enforcing 8pp is a mislabeled claim.
evidence: code/test_provenance_smoke.py:62 `assert abs(ri - chance) < 8.0`; line 63 message `within ~3pp of chance`; sample count from DummyLoader(10,10) at lines 52-54 and n_seeds=2 at line 59.
fix: Pick one tolerance, justify it from the sample size, and make the printed message match the asserted bound. Either raise the message to ~8pp or tighten the assert to ~3pp AND increase the DummyLoader sample count so ~3pp is statistically defensible.

title: The 'key assertion' is not an assertion — it is a non-enforcing if/else that always passes
description: The comment on lines 87-88 calls the near-chance zero-shot check 'The key assertion', but lines 89-93 implement it as an `if abs(...) < 3.0: print(ok) else: print(warning)` — it never fails the test. The module still prints 'SMOKE TEST PASSED' (line 109) regardless of whether SHD zero-shot is near chance. So the single most important property this smoke test claims to verify (no spurious cross-modal signal / no data leakage) is not enforced. Compounding it, the 3.0 pp band is tighter than the noise floor of a ~40-sample evaluate() (DummyLoader(10,20), line 53), so the warning branch fires often yet nothing fails.
evidence: code/test_provenance_smoke.py:87-88 comment 'The key assertion'; lines 89-93 if/else that only prints; line 109 prints PASSED unconditionally; evaluate() sample count ~40 from dummy_shd = DummyLoader(10, 20) at line 53.
fix: Promote the check to a real assertion (assert abs(acc_shd_zero - chance_shd) < TOL) with a defensible TOL and larger sample count, or explicitly document why it is only a warning. Do not label a warning as the 'key assertion'.

title: Hardcoded accuracy-like literals passed into print_task_sanity
description: The print_task_sanity call is fed fabricated numbers: after_training_acc=15.0 (line 103), learning_gain=15.0 - acc_shd_zero (line 104), random_init_baseline_acc=5.2 (line 105). These are placeholder literals, not measured quantities. Because this is a smoke test and the values are only printed (never written to a results CSV), the impact is low, but hardcoded accuracy-shaped numbers (15.0, 5.2) in a file whose output is labeled 'SANITY' are exactly the pattern RULE 1 warns against, and a reader skimming stdout could mistake them for measurements.
evidence: code/test_provenance_smoke.py:103 after_training_acc=15.0; line 104 learning_gain=15.0 - acc_shd_zero; line 105 random_init_baseline_acc=5.2.
fix: Either drive print_task_sanity from actually-computed values, or clearly comment these as dummy placeholders in the smoke path so they cannot be mistaken for results.

title: Unused import numpy as np
description: numpy is imported (line 7) but never referenced anywhere in the file (no `np.` usage). Dead import.
evidence: code/test_provenance_smoke.py:7 `import numpy as np`; grep for `np.` in the file returns no usage.
fix: Remove the unused import.

title: DummyLoader hardcodes batch size 4 and tensor shapes, ignoring cfg.batch_size
description: DummyLoader.__iter__ hardcodes a batch dimension of 4 and fixed tensor shapes (lines 44-48) while cfg.batch_size is also set to 4 (line 27). The two are coupled only by coincidence: changing cfg.batch_size would not change the batches the loader yields, so the config knob is silently ignored. The magic shapes ([4,25,2,34,34] and [4,100,1,1,700]) are also duplicated from the real dataset specs without a named constant.
evidence: code/test_provenance_smoke.py:44 `x = torch.randn(4, 25, 2, 34, 34)`; line 46 `x = torch.randn(4, 100, 1, 1, 700)`; line 47 `y = torch.randint(0, self.n_classes, (4,))`; cfg.batch_size=4 at line 27.
fix: Parameterize DummyLoader by batch size (pass cfg.batch_size) or assert/comment that the fixed 4 is intentional; name the modality shapes as constants.

title: Zero-shot section is not seeded, so its outcome is not reproducible by design
description: The test never calls torch.manual_seed / np.random.seed in its own body. The model constructed at line 68 and the training at lines 73-78 consume whatever global RNG state is left over from the preceding random_init_baseline loop (which reseeds internally to cfg.seed+1000+s, lines 58-62). So the zero-shot accuracy that feeds the near-chance check (lines 81-93) depends on incidental RNG ordering, not on a declared seed. Combined with the tight/under-powered tolerances, pass/warn behavior is not reproducible across code changes that alter earlier RNG consumption.
evidence: No torch.manual_seed/np.random.seed in code/test_provenance_smoke.py; model init at line 68 follows random_init_baseline reseeding at lines 58-62; zero-shot check at lines 89-93.
fix: Set torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed) and np.random.seed(cfg.seed) at the start of the zero-shot block (or the test function) so the result is deterministic and reproducible.

title: Entire alignment smoke test executes at import time (no __main__ guard, no functions)
description: Like the provenance smoke test, there is no __main__ guard and no functions; the body (model build line 75, forward passes lines 86-96, orthogonal/SupCon checks lines 103-115, a 2-epoch alignment run lines 130-138, and 3 optimizer steps lines 152-157) all execute on import. Import==execution. VERIFIED SAFE from the 4-5h trap: device='cpu' (line 58), FakePairedDataset random tensors (lines 26-40), and it imports only m7_trimodal_run_provenance (guarded) plus Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader — not the unguarded m7_trimodal_run. But collecting/importing it still runs real backprop and can error during collection.
evidence: No `if __name__`/`def ` (only class FakePairedDataset and methods); executable top-level statements lines 67-169; device cpu at line 58; align_cross_modal 2-epoch run at lines 130-138.
fix: Move the body into test_* functions with a __main__ guard so import/collection does not run training.

title: Flaky assertion: cross-modal loss must strictly decrease over just 2 epochs on near-noise fake data
description: Line 142 asserts history['xmscl_loss'][1] < history['xmscl_loss'][0] — i.e. the CrossModalSupCon loss must strictly drop between epoch 1 and epoch 2. The data is FakePairedDataset, where per-class signal is c*0.05 added onto randn*0.1 noise (lines 37-39), i.e. mostly noise; optimization uses AdamW with CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=num_epochs=2) (m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:702). Over only two epochs on near-noise data a strict monotonic decrease is not guaranteed, so this test can fail spuriously on some seeds/runs — a false alarm rather than a real regression signal.
evidence: code/test_cross_modal_alignment.py:142-143 strict `<` assertion; FakePairedDataset signal c*0.05 over 0.1 noise at lines 37-39; num_epochs=2 at line 132; CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=num_epochs) in align_cross_modal (m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:702).
fix: Make the check robust: assert loss[-1] <= loss[0] with a tolerance, or assert a downward trend over more epochs, or compare mean of last-half vs first-half. Seed the run and/or increase epochs so the trend is reliable.

title: Local TASKS is a hand-copied duplicate of the canonical module-level TASKS (silent-drift risk)
description: The test defines its own TASKS dict (lines 61-65) instead of importing the canonical TASKS from m7_trimodal_run_provenance (lines 955-959). The two are byte-for-byte equivalent TODAY (nmnist:10/visual, shd:20/audio, dvs:11/visual_motion), so there is no current bug, but it is a duplicated source of truth: if the real TASKS schema or class counts change, this test keeps building the model against a stale task spec and will not detect the drift. (Note: it is not literal Python shadowing, since this file does not import TASKS — it is a divergent copy.)
evidence: code/test_cross_modal_alignment.py:61-65 local TASKS; identical structure to m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:955-959.
fix: Import TASKS from m7_trimodal_run_provenance and use it, or build the test's TASKS from that source, so there is a single source of truth.

title: Vacuous assertions that are true by construction and validate nothing
description: Two assertions cannot meaningfully fail. Line 105 `assert pen.item() >= 0` — orthogonal_penalty returns cross.pow(2).sum() (m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:218-219), a sum of squares, which is always >= 0. Line 114 `assert loss_xmscl.item() > 0` — a SupCon loss is a mean of non-negative -log_prob terms and is essentially always positive. These checks only confirm the calls return a scalar; they give no evidence the quantities are correct. The scalar-ness checks (lines 104, 113 `ndim == 0`) are fine but weak.
evidence: code/test_cross_modal_alignment.py:105 `assert pen.item() >= 0`; orthogonal_penalty sum-of-squares at m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:218-219; line 114 `assert loss_xmscl.item() > 0`.
fix: Replace tautological bounds with checks that could fail: e.g. penalty of orthogonalized vs correlated inputs differs as expected; SupCon loss decreases when identical-label embeddings are made more similar; or compare against a known reference value.

title: Orthogonal-penalty test uses a raw slice, not the model's learned proj_private
description: private_vis is computed by slicing full_vis[:, cfg.align_shared_dim:] (line 102), i.e. the tail dimensions of the full feature, whereas the model's actual private subspace is a learned nn.Linear projection self.proj_private (m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:339). So the penalty exercised here is on a different quantity than the one the model uses in training, and (given the vacuous >=0 assertion, TST-012) the test would not catch a bug in proj_private wiring. It validates orthogonal_penalty's arithmetic but not the model's shared/private split.
evidence: code/test_cross_modal_alignment.py:102 `private_vis = full_vis[:, cfg.align_shared_dim:]`; model's proj_private is a learned Linear at m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:339.
fix: Obtain private from the model's proj_private path (or from the model's own split helper) so the test reflects what training actually uses, and add a meaningful assertion on it.

title: Unused import numpy as np
description: numpy is imported (line 11) but never used in the file (no `np.` reference). Dead import.
evidence: code/test_cross_modal_alignment.py:11 `import numpy as np`; grep for `np.` returns no usage.
fix: Remove the unused import.

title: Imports placed mid-module, relying on the second sys.path hack
description: `from torch.utils.data import DataLoader` (line 123) and `from Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader import paired_digit_collate_fn` (line 124) appear in the middle of the executable body rather than with the other imports at the top. Dataset was already imported at line 12, so the mid-file DataLoader import is redundant-adjacent, and the Dataloaders import depends on the repo-root sys.path.insert at line 8 (the file has no code/ package). This is fragile and hurts readability; if the body is later refactored into functions these buried imports are easy to miss.
evidence: code/test_cross_modal_alignment.py:123 mid-file DataLoader import; line 124 Dataloaders import; repo-root path inserted at line 8; torch.utils.data.Dataset imported at top (line 12).
fix: Move both imports to the top import block; keep the sys.path.insert but consolidate imports so the dependency on it is explicit.

title: ImportError on import: _build_digit_loaders is not exported by run_ordinal_anchor
description: The test does `from run_ordinal_anchor import (..., _build_digit_loaders, ...)` (line 14), but run_ordinal_anchor neither defines nor re-exports _build_digit_loaders. That symbol is defined in run_correspondence_anchor_v2.py (line 67); run_ordinal_anchor imports several helpers from that module (lines 51-58: _hash_params, _load_cached_features, build_paired_feature_dataset, compute_held_out_metrics, run_procrustes, train_correspondence) but NOT _build_digit_loaders. run_ordinal_anchor only defines a differently-named _build_test_loaders (line 75). Result: `ImportError: cannot import name '_build_digit_loaders' from 'run_ordinal_anchor'`. The module raises before main() ever runs, so the __main__ guard is moot and this is the actual, live crash — earlier than the missing-data/checkpoint issues.
evidence: code/test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py:14 imports _build_digit_loaders from run_ordinal_anchor; run_ordinal_anchor.py:51-58 import list omits it; _build_digit_loaders defined in run_correspondence_anchor_v2.py:67; run_ordinal_anchor.py:75 defines only _build_test_loaders.
fix: Import _build_digit_loaders from run_correspondence_anchor_v2 (where it lives), or add it to run_ordinal_anchor's re-export block (run_ordinal_anchor.py:51-58). Confirm the intended loader: run_ordinal_anchor exposes _build_test_loaders, which may be the one actually wanted.

title: Requires N-MNIST/SHD datasets not in the repo — becomes a large tonic download once the import is fixed
description: main() calls _build_digit_loaders(cfg) (line 61). That builder (run_correspondence_anchor_v2.py:67-91) constructs tonic.datasets.NMNIST and SHD with save_to='./ICONS_M7/datasets' and mkdir(parents=True) — the repo has no ICONS_M7 datasets (per CLAUDE.md/AUDIT_SPEC). So once TST-016 is fixed, running this file will trigger a multi-GB tonic dataset DOWNLOAD (or crash if offline), and the path is CWD-relative so it only resolves as intended when run from code/. Today this is masked by the ImportError (TST-016), which is why severity is medium rather than a live download; but any naive 'fix the import and run it' will hit the download.
evidence: code/test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py:61 `loaders = _build_digit_loaders(cfg)`; run_correspondence_anchor_v2.py:67-91 build NMNIST/SHD via tonic with save_to='./ICONS_M7/datasets' and data_dir.mkdir; repo has no ICONS_M7 datasets.
fix: For a true smoke test, feed a tiny fake/dummy paired loader (as test_cross_modal_alignment.py does with FakePairedDataset) instead of _build_digit_loaders, or gate the real-data path behind an explicit env flag / pytest skip so it never downloads unexpectedly.

title: Requires a cached-feature artifact and a checkpoint that do not exist in the repo
description: main() calls _load_cached_features(device) (line 64) and run_one_seed(42, cfg, loaders, cached, device, head_type='mlp') (line 73). run_one_seed (run_ordinal_anchor.py:395-411) does torch.load(CKPT_SOURCE) where CKPT_SOURCE = REPO_ROOT/results/cl_confirmation/checkpoints/A_no_align_seed42/final_shd_shd.pt (run_ordinal_anchor.py:63-70). The repo has no results/ directory and no *.pt checkpoints, and _load_cached_features expects a cached feature file. So even past TST-016 and TST-017, this crashes with FileNotFoundError on the missing checkpoint/cache. Masked today by TST-016.
evidence: code/test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py:64 `_load_cached_features(device)`; line 73 run_one_seed(...); torch.load(CKPT_SOURCE) at run_ordinal_anchor.py:410; CKPT_SOURCE path at run_ordinal_anchor.py:63-70; verified no results/ dir and no *.pt in repo.
fix: For a smoke test, provide a tiny synthetic cached-feature dict and either construct a fresh model instead of loading CKPT_SOURCE or point at a small fixture checkpoint; otherwise mark the test skip when the artifacts are absent so it degrades gracefully.

title: Has a __main__ guard and main() (good) but still not a pytest test and asserts almost nothing
description: Unlike the other two, this file correctly wraps its logic in main() (line 22) under an `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard (line 83), so importing it does not run the body. But it defines no test_* function (pytest collects 0 items — see TST-001), and its only 'assertion' is a print of 'Smoke test passed.' (line 80) with no assert statements at all: it just runs run_one_seed and prints results. Even if it ran, it would validate nothing programmatically. It is a manual demo script, not a test.
evidence: code/test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py:22 def main(); line 83 __main__ guard; line 80 prints 'Smoke test passed.'; no `assert` anywhere in the file.
fix: Rename to a run_/demo_ script if it is meant to be run manually, OR convert to real pytest test_* functions with concrete assertions (e.g. on rdm keys, res dict fields) and dummy inputs so it can live in the validation loop.

title: Inline ExperimentConfig duplicates the full production hyperparameter set
description: The test hand-writes a 34-field ExperimentConfig (lines 23-56) restating essentially all M7 production hyperparameters (num_patterns=100, time_steps=25, beta=0.9, hidden_dim=512, shared_dim=512, contrastive_temperature=0.07, replay_weight=0.3, etc.). Most are already the dataclass defaults (m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:34-74), so this is redundant, and it is a second place these production values are pinned — if the real defaults change, this smoke config silently diverges. A smoke test should use small/cheap values (small dims, few epochs), not mirror the full production config.
evidence: code/test_ordinal_anchor_smoke.py:23-56 inline ExperimentConfig with production values; same fields/defaults defined in m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:34-74.
fix: Only override the fields the smoke test needs (and make them small); rely on dataclass defaults for the rest. Avoid re-pinning production hyperparameters in a test.

title: Verified: importing the two top-level smoke tests does NOT trigger the 4-5h run or a dataset download
description: Guidance for whoever fixes these. Statically verified that test_provenance_smoke.py and test_cross_modal_alignment.py only import m7_trimodal_run_provenance (and, for the latter, Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader). m7_trimodal_run_provenance is __main__-guarded (m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:1378), performs no dataset load / mkdir / DataLoader construction at module scope, and does NOT import the unguarded m7_trimodal_run. Both tests force device='cpu' and use synthetic loaders. Therefore they are safe to move into tests/ and run under `pytest tests/` after being wrapped in test_ functions. This is the opposite of the dangerous code/m7_trimodal_run.py, which must never be imported. The ordinal smoke test is also safe to import (its heavy work is behind main()), but it raises ImportError immediately (TST-016).
evidence: m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py:1378 __main__ guard; no module-level tonic.datasets/mkdir/DataLoader in that file; it does not import m7_trimodal_run; device cpu at test_provenance_smoke.py:31 and test_cross_modal_alignment.py:58.
fix: No action required. Use this when relocating the dataset-free smoke tests into tests/ per TST-001.
